question: Organic fields yield less on average. If a field grows a quarter less, how much more land does the same loaf need?
answer: A third more, not a quarter. Land per tonne is one divided by yield, so each extra point of yield gap costs more land than the last. A 2012 analysis in Nature found organic yields about 25% lower on average. Fewer chemicals per field can still mean more ploughed or cleared land per loaf.
move: Judge a method per unit of what it makes, not per field.
ask: Am I measuring my choices per item, when what matters is the total result?
reference: Seufert, Ramankutty & Foley, Comparing the yields of organic and conventional agriculture, Nature, 2012

notes.text: 5% lower, as for some legumes: barely more land.
The average gap, 25%: a third more land, not a quarter.
34% lower, the strictest comparisons: half as much land again.
Half the yield: twice the land.
